title: feat(web): developer-only feature flag editor
description:
## What it solves

No way to locally toggle the feature flags the web app gets from the config service without changing the service or rebuilding.

## How this PR fixes it

A **dev/staging-only** editor that stores per-flag overrides in the browser and applies them instantly across all chains, no reload. It opens as a dialog from the sidebar's Developer group — there is no route.

- Persisted `featureFlagOverrides` slice + a pure `applyFeatureOverrides` helper wired into `useChain` / `useChains` / `useCurrentChain`, so all ~134 `useHasFeature` consumers and every route/nav gate inherit overrides automatically.
- The sidebar gained **action items** — entries that run a callback instead of navigating — since this one has no route. `ResolvedSidebarItem` is now a discriminated union, so the compiler enforces that nav items always carry a link.
- **Production exclusion:** `FeatureFlagEditorDialogLoader` is the single boundary, wrapping `dynamic(() => import(...))` in an inlined `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_PRODUCTION === 'true'` check so the editor graph is dead-code-eliminated. The feature's `index.ts` barrel is deleted — it re-exported the editor and was a live static path into that graph. `applyFeatureOverrides` is also a hard prod no-op, so hand-edited `localStorage` cannot flip flags in production.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/abfbfb97-7a68-4a70-991c-6f673aba8025

## How to test it

1. In dev, open any Safe → sidebar **Developer → Feature flags** → toggle a flag (e.g. `EARN`). Nav/route/feature UI update instantly, no reload; the sidebar badge tracks the override count; overrides survive reload.
2. `/feature-flags` should 404 — the route is gone.
3. `yarn workspace @safe-global/web test src/features/feature-flags src/hooks/useChains.test.ts src/features/spaces/components/Sidebar`
4. Prod exclusion: `RUN_BUNDLE_TESTS=true yarn workspace @safe-global/web test bundleExclusion`

## Affected flows

- Local override → global, reload-free effect on nav visibility, route gating, and feature UI.
- Dev-only Developer sidebar group opening the dialog (hidden entirely in production).
- Every sidebar entry in both the Safe and Spaces sidebars now flows through the nav/action union in `NavItem`.

## Blast radius

- **Shared chain hooks** (`useChains.ts`) — ~134 `useHasFeature` consumers plus route/nav gating; behaviour-preserving with no overrides.
- **Sidebar types** — `ResolvedSidebarItem` union, consumed by the main nav, Settings, the DeFi group, and the Spaces sidebar. `useResolvedSidebarNav` lost its developer-group parameter; the other caller is unaffected.
- **Store** — new persisted `featureFlagOverridesSlice`.
- **Routing** — `/feature-flags` and `AppRoutes.featureFlags` removed, no redirect; existing bookmarks 404.
- **Mobile** — no mobile-app changes (web-only). Mobile *web* drawer fixed: dismissing it no longer unmounts the component owning the dialog's state.

## Risks / not checked

- `bundleExclusion.test.ts` is the only end-to-end proof the editor is absent from production chunks, and it **runs in no CI job** (`RUN_BUNDLE_TESTS` appears nowhere in `.github/`). Validated locally on this branch against a real production `next build`; nothing currently stops a future regression.
- The loader's guard test pins the `process.env` comparison but not the `dynamic()` import shape — a rewrite to a static import with the same guard would still pass the unit tests.
- The mobile drawer fix is unit-covered only; no integration test mounts the real `SheetContent` portal at phone width.
- Chains read straight from the store (not via the hooks) don't see overrides. Route/nav gating uses the hooks, so it is covered.
- The feature intentionally has **no `index.ts`**, unlike every other feature — the barrel was a production-leak path. Deliberate deviation from `docs/feature-architecture.md`.

## Checklist

- [x] I've tested the branch on mobile 📱 — web-only; mobile-web drawer interaction fixed and unit-tested
- [x] I've documented how it affects the analytics (if at all) 📊 — action items still emit `SIDEBAR_CLICKED`; no new events
- [x] I've written a unit/e2e test for it (if applicable) 🧑‍💻
- [x] I've listed affected flows and blast radius, and named what I did not verify 🎯

findings.claim: A doc comment on useFeatureFlagEditorData explaining that its data is deliberately un-overridden would clarify the design intent.
tabIndex={isOverridden ? undefined : -1} is placed inside a block that already only renders when isOverridden is true, so the -1 branch of the ternary can never execute.
When a search matches no rows, the section components return null, leaving the page blank below the toolbar with no 'no matching flags' message for the user.
Either sr-only text alongside the visible check should be used for reliable accessibility, or the aria-label on the icon should be dropped since the TooltipContent already carries the announcement.

The featureFlagOverridesSlice reducer is registered unconditionally and included in persistedSlices and broadcastState, so the reducer, persisted state, and broadcast channel ship in production even though applyFeatureOverrides is a no-op there.
A stale featureFlagOverrides localStorage entry, for example left over from prior staging use on the same origin, will silently persist in production forever with no UI to clear it.
The new components are flat files directly under components/ instead of following the project's convention of one folder per component containing an index.tsx with its test and story alongside it.

Several long Tailwind class strings with custom values (a multi-part before: accent bar, an exported GRID constant with custom grid-cols shared across files, and a header with custom text sizing) should be moved into named classes in a CSS module instead of being inlined, which would also remove the need for the exported string constant.

The tooltip trigger uses visibility: hidden with an aria-label, but visibility: hidden removes the element from the accessibility tree as well as from hit-testing, so the aria-label and tooltip content are never announced to screen reader users even when matchesCurrentChain is true.

The hook reads only the data from the config query and ignores isLoading and error, so when the config service fails every flag renders as 'Off' with no indication that loading failed, and toggling a flag in that state saves an override based on invalid or missing config.

This file checks process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_PRODUCTION directly instead of using the IS_PRODUCTION constant from @/config/constants, and unlike the other two places that do this, it has no build-time pruning reason to bypass the shared constant.

The feature's barrel file exports only the implementation component and has no feature.ts or createFeatureHandle, deviating from how other features expose themselves; if intentional (to allow the editor to be dropped from production via dynamic import) this deviation should be noted in the PR description so it isn't copied as the normal pattern for other features.

No test covers the editor's interactions, including search filtering, the 'Reset all overrides' action and its disabled state, a switch toggle calling setOverride, a revert action calling clearOverride, and a section hiding itself when it has no matching rows.

The hook only reads data from useGetChainsConfigV2Query and ignores isLoading and error, so while the request is loading or if it fails, chains defaults to an empty array and every row displays an 'Off' badge and a false config value as if it were real data.

The prop tabIndex={isOverridden ? undefined : -1} sits inside a block already gated on isOverridden being true, so the -1 branch can never execute, making the ternary dead code that should be simplified.

The production check process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_PRODUCTION === 'true' is written inline in multiple places (also in SafeSidebarContent.tsx) instead of reusing the shared IS_PRODUCTION constant from config/constants.ts, and the sidebar copy has no comment explaining why it needs the inline form.
Test chains are constructed by hand and cast with (...) as unknown as Chain instead of using the existing chainBuilder helper, which would produce a fully typed chain and avoid the double type cast.

The editor's rows show the raw config-service value in configValue and chainScope while useHasFeature and everything gated by it reflect the overridden value, so the 'Config service' column does not reflect overrides even though the switch below it does; this intentional split is not documented.
The story titles use the prefix 'FeatureFlags/...' instead of the 'Features/FeatureFlags/...' pattern used by other feature stories and specified in apps/web/AGENTS.md.
The alignment spacer is a bit magic and, despite an existing comment on the grid, could get lost or become confusing in future edits.

When the new switch value equals row.configValue, clearOverride(feature) should be dispatched instead of setOverride, matching the behavior of the revert-override control, and the corresponding test file should be updated to cover this case.

The marker string "local feature-flag overrides" used in the bundle exclusion test is generic enough that an unrelated future copy change could accidentally satisfy or invalidate the test, so a more distinctive, editor-only sentinel string or a dedicated data attribute should be used instead.
Sorting is done inline via localeCompare on every render even though FEATURES is a fixed enum, so alphabetizing once at module scope would avoid redundant re-sorting.
The feature has no contract.ts, feature.ts, or createFeatureHandle, which docs/feature-architecture.md requires for features, though other features in the codebase also skip this pattern.
The Developer group block is almost a copy of the DeFi group block a few lines above it, duplicating the same structure rather than sharing it.

selectOverrideCount subscribes the sidebar to the store in production even though the feature flag group is hidden there; hoisting the IS_PRODUCTION check above useAppSelector would avoid this, though it requires a conditional-hook pattern and the current cost is negligible.

The only test verifying the editor stays out of production builds is skipped unless the RUN_BUNDLE_TESTS environment variable is set, and nothing in the workflows or scripts sets that variable, so a break in the production-exclusion guard would not be caught by CI.
There is no unit test for FeatureFlagSection verifying it returns null when rows.length is 0.

Code inside the feature-flags feature imports its own store using the absolute path @/features/feature-flags/store while the same files use relative imports for everything else, so the feature does not follow one consistent import style.
There is no unit test for FeatureFlagEditor covering the search filter, the 'Reset all overrides' button's enable/disable state and dispatch, and the empty overridden section.
There is no test verifying that applyFeatureOverrides correctly handles a chain with an override for a feature not present in the Chain['features'] enum type, even though the cast to string is safe.

The switch's onCheckedChange always dispatches setOverride even when the new value equals the config value, so toggling a row off and back on leaves it marked as an override (shown as matching the current chain) instead of returning to a clean, non-overridden state, causing users to accumulate silent overrides.
When a search matches no flags, both sections return null, leaving the area under the search box blank instead of showing a message like other list views in the app do for zero results.
The folder name feature-flags should be renamed to something else, as the current name may not be appropriate or clear.
